text:
Terrible. The doctor said one thing, the staff outside said another. The doctor quoted a total price for the dental work, but the staff outside said it wasn't included yet. Couldn't they have agreed on that beforehand? I waited from 9 am until 2 pm.

Then, when it was time to schedule the appointment:
Staff: "Which day is convenient for you?"
Patient: "Okay."
Staff: "Or maybe the 15th or the 20th? Which day is convenient?"
"Okay, that was fine from the first day. Why keep changing it?"
Staff: "That day is very busy. It's probably not possible then."
"So, what day is available? Just say it clearly and let me know."
The paperwork was also a mess. They asked for documents, and I was asked if they were necessary. Why ask for them if you don't need them? So frustrating!

restaurant_name: ธิตินันท์ทันตคลินิก
text: The dentist was kind, lovely, and chatted with us to ease our fear. She was gentle and gave very detailed advice on dental care. However, there was a bit of a wait, but that's understandable given the large number of patients. The staff outside the clinic were also helpful. (It's convenient because it's close to our house.) 👍 …

restaurant_name: ธิตินันท์ทันตคลินิก
text: I went for orthodontic treatment three years ago. The dentist was lovely; I was lucky to have a female doctor, probably in her late 20s, who was very sweet and hummed songs while doing my teeth. Dr. Thitinan was very kind. But the problem was the grumpy old lady at the counter. She wrote the appointment slip incorrectly almost 10 times. She just checked the schedule for the doctor's availability and still got it wrong. It was so frustrating. I arrived and she said, "The doctor isn't here today," laughing to cover her embarrassment. She never apologized, just gave a forced laugh (I guess she thought it was funny). Dr. Thitinan apologized, saying, "I'm sorry, the staff wrote the appointment date wrong." But...the doctor apologized, yet the staff member didn't apologize at all. I was so confused. She just kept asking where I lived and if it was far. "Oh, but it's still in the district," I said. It doesn't matter where I live! The point is, I drove all this way, wasting gas, and all this for nothing? Not a single apology, just a forced laugh. Should I pay for your gas, you ghost?!
